newsitem.title: USA: U.S., UK report progress in talks on new air pact.
newsitem.headline: U.S., UK report progress in talks on new air pact.

text.p: The United States and Britain on Friday reported progress in a round of talks over the past three days toward a new free-market "open skies" aviation agreement.

John Byerly, a State Department negotiator, said after the negotiations that "the two delegations concurred that the talks had been useful and that the two sides had made progress toward an agreed text for a new bilateral accord."

The talks held Tuesday through Thursday were to write a new agreement to replace the existing restrictive bilateral aviation services accord. Previous talks had been held on and off the past two years, with little progress reported.
Byerly did not detail the issues settled and said some were unresolved, added: "The delegates achieved a fuller understanding of their respective positions."

A major issue blocking an agreement has been Britain's reluctance to cede additional landing slots at London's Heathrow airport, considered by American carriers to be a key transfer point for flights beyond Britain to continental Europe. Heathrow is dominated by British Airways Plc..

The U.S.-British talks are being closely watched by American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp., and BA because the United States has said it would not approve the alliance they have proposed unless a free market aviation agreement was first reached.
